summary: Deep-copies a null-terminated array of string pointers. Walks the input array counting elements until a null terminator, allocates 4 * (count + 1) bytes, aborts via CRTAmsgExit(9) if allocation fails, then copies each entry through StringAllocCopy and null-terminates the new array. Returns the newly allocated array, or 0 when the input pointer is null.

operations.description: If the input array pointer a1 is null, return 0 immediately.

Walk a1 + 1 through the array elements (starting at the element after the first, i.e. the int at offset 4) until a null entry is found, counting entries as they are read; the first element read comes from field at offset 0.
Allocate 4 * count + 4 bytes for the copy array via MallocWrapperForNhMalloc.
If the allocation returned null, terminate the process via CRTAmsgExit(9).
While the current source element is non-null, deep-copy it through StringAllocCopy into the destination and advance both the source element pointer and the destination pointer.
Write a null terminator after the last copied entry.
Return the base pointer of the newly allocated copied array.

unresolved: Structure of the objects returned by StringAllocCopy is unknown; only the containing null-terminated array is reconstructed.
Meaning of the CRTAmsgExit(9) exit code 9 is unresolved.
The field offsets 0 and 4 are the first two int slots of the walked array, but their per-entry semantics are caller-defined.
